mainEntity.name: What engines came in the Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Passat 2.0 TSI has been offered with several engine codes across generations. B6 / B7 (2008-2014): CAWB, CCZA (200hp), later 210hp. B8 (2015-2019): CHHB (220hp, 350Nm). B8 (2017-2020): CZPA (190hp). B8 facelift (2019-2024): DNNA (190hp, EA888 evo4).

mainEntity.name: Does the Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 TSI (EA888) uses a timing chain, not a belt. Early models (2008-2012) are known for timing chain tensioner failure. The original tensioner (06H-109-467) was updated to a revised design (06K-109-467) from 2012 onwards. If you hear a rattle on cold start, have the tensioner inspected immediately. Timing chain - not a belt. Early tensioner (06H-109-467) is prone to failure. Updated tensioner (06K-109-467) is more reliable. Rattle on cold start is a warning sign.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 TSI is generally reliable when properly maintained, but it has known issues: timing chain tensioner (pre-2012) - prone to failure - replace proactively; oil consumption - piston ring design can cause oil burning; carbon buildup - direct-injection causes intake valve deposits; water pump - can fail, causing coolant loss. Regular maintenance with the correct oil and proactive replacement of known weak points will ensure long-term reliability.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement for a Passat 2.0 TSI typically costs £1,800-£4,200 supply-only, depending on the engine code and condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt). Full supply & fit through a specialist adds approximately £700-£1,200 in labour. Used CAWB: £750-£1,400. Reconditioned CHHB: £1,800-£3,000. Rebuilt CHHB: £2,500-£4,000. Rebuilt DNNA: £2,600-£4,200. Fitting labour: 10-14 hours at £65/hr indie rates.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Passat 2.0 TSI engine swap takes 2-5 working days, depending on the workshop's workload and whether supply-only or supply & fit is chosen. Supply-only: 1-3 days for delivery. Supply & fit: 3-5 days total (including delivery and fitting). Mobile fitting: may take longer as the fitter travels to your location.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI petrol engine arrived with the B7 generation in 2010 as part of the EA888 family, replacing the earlier 2.0 FSI. Over its production life, the 2.0 TSI received multiple updates across the B7 and B8 generations, with power outputs ranging from 210hp to 220hp and later 190hp in the evo4 iteration.

milestones.description: B7 Passat launches with 2.0 TSI (EA888 Gen 2), 210hp, 280Nm torque
Timing chain tensioner updated to revised design (06K-109-467) addressing early failure concerns
B8 Passat introduces EA888 Gen 3 2.0 TSI (CHHB), 220hp, 350Nm torque
B8 facelift; 2.0 TSI 190hp (CZPA/DKZA) introduced alongside 220hp variants
EA888 evo4 (DNNA) introduced with 190hp, improved efficiency and durability
B9 Passat launches with 1.5 eTSI and eHybrid only - 2.0 TSI petrol discontinued in UK

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Passat 2.0 TSI is a powerful and refined engine, but several failure patterns have emerged across the EA888 family. **Timing chain tensioner failure** on early models, **oil consumption** due to piston ring design, and **carbon buildup** on intake valves are the most commonly reported issues. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Early Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI Fails Catastrophically
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI (CAWB, CCZA, early CHHB), 2008-2013
problems.rootCause: The original timing chain tensioner (06H-109-467) fitted to early EA888 engines has a plastic collar that can fail, allowing the tensioner piston to retract. When the engine is off, oil pressure drops, and the chain can loosen. This can cause the chain to skip timing, leading to pistons and valves colliding - catastrophic engine damage. The issue was addressed with an updated tensioner (06K-109-467) from 2012 onwards.

repairOptions.longevity: Preventative - recommended if old tensioner is fitted

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain kit including tensioner, guides and chain
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if chain is stretched or guides are worn
Only if chain failure has caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Passat 2.0 TSI (2008-2016) is worth approximately £3,000-£15,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. Timing chain replacement (£500-£1,400 specialist) is a significant but justifiable expense for most examples. For vehicles under £3,000, carefully evaluate whether the repair makes sense.
problems.recommendation: If your Passat 2.0 TSI has the old tensioner (06H-109-467), replace it proactively with the updated version (06K-109-467). The timing chain cover has an inspection hole to check which tensioner is fitted. Ignoring a rattling noise on cold start can lead to a £3,000+ engine replacement.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Why the Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: A class action lawsuit alleges that the piston rings in EA888 2.0 TSI engines do not maintain sufficient tension, permitting oil to enter the combustion chamber. Burning oil leads to carbon buildup that damages the PCV valve, while increased crankcase pressure causes gaskets and seals to fail. Symptoms include frequent oil top-ups between service intervals, fouled spark plugs, and blue smoke from the exhaust.

repairOptions.longevity: May reduce oil consumption if PCV is faulty
The definitive fix - eliminates oil consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, full engine replacement with upgraded piston rings

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Passat worth over £5,000, piston ring replacement (£1,800-£3,000 specialist) is a worthwhile investment. For vehicles under £4,000, a used engine may be more cost-effective.
problems.recommendation: Monitor your oil level regularly. If you're adding more than 1 litre of oil per 1,000 miles, have the engine inspected. A faulty PCV valve is a cheaper fix - replace it first. If consumption persists, piston ring replacement or a rebuilt engine with upgraded rings is the definitive solution.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why the Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI Loses Power and Idles Roughly
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Passat 2.0 TSI (all direct-injection EA888 variants)
problems.rootCause: Direct-injection petrol engines do not have fuel washing over the intake valves, allowing carbon deposits to build up over time. Symptoms include rough idle, reduced performance, hesitation on acceleration, and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits

repairOptions.specialistPrice: N/A (carbon buildup alone does not justify full replacement)
repairOptions.longevity: Carbon buildup is a maintenance issue, not a replacement trigger

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Carbon cleaning (£400-£800 specialist) is well within the value of any Passat 2.0 TSI.
problems.recommendation: If your Passat 2.0 TSI feels sluggish or has a rough idle, carbon cleaning is a cost-effective solution. Use premium fuel and occasional "Italian tune-ups" to help reduce the rate of carbon buildup.
